title: Open strong
learn: Start with a hook: a question, a short story or a surprising fact.

pages.title: Open strong
pages.body: Ever wonder how to grab someone's attention right away? Great openings make people want to listen to what you have to say.
pages.learn: Start with a hook: a question, a short story or a surprising fact.

steps.label: Start with hook
steps.text: Open with a question, a short story, or a surprising fact to capture interest.

steps.label: Keep it relevant
steps.text: Your attention-getter must connect to your speech topic and purpose.

steps.label: Be concrete/novel
steps.text: The best attention getters are real, new, or familiar to the audience.

steps.label: Establish trust
steps.text: Let the audience know why you are a knowledgeable source on the topic.

terms.meaning: A device used at the beginning to capture the audience's interest.

A brief account or story of an interesting or humorous event.

pages.title: Before and after
pages.situation: Introducing a speech on saving money.
pages.before: Hi, my name is Alex, and today I want to talk to you about saving money.
pages.after: What if I told you that small daily changes could change your future? I'm here to share how to save money.
pages.why: The new version uses a question to immediately capture attention.

pages.title: Why it works
pages.body: Starting with a hook, like a question, makes the audience interested in your topic right away, instead of just stating your name.

cite.book: Stand up, Speak out: The Practice and Ethics of Public Speaking (UWM edition)
cite.chapter: The Basis for Strong Public Speaking

quiz.q: If you are using a short story to grab attention, what is the most important rule to follow?
options: It must be very long to be convincing.
It needs to connect directly to your speech topic.
It should be completely unrelated to the topic for surprise.
quiz.explain: The attention-getter must connect to your speech topic.

quiz.q: Which of the following best describes a 'Rhetorical Question' as an attention-getter?
options: A question that requires the audience to give a detailed answer.
A question asked to make the audience think, but not expecting a reply.
A question that only relates to the speaker's personal life.
quiz.explain: A rhetorical question is asked where no actual reply is expected.

quiz.q: When choosing an attention-getter, what quality makes it most effective?
options: It must be extremely formal and academic.
It should be real, new, or familiar to the audience.
It must always be a surprising fact, no matter what.
quiz.explain: The best attention getters are real, new, or familiar to the audience.

examples.student: Did you know that 80% of students struggle with procrastination? I’ve spent the last semester researching productivity hacks, and I found three surprisingly effective techniques that actually work for real people.
examples.job_seeker: Imagine a moment where a critical deadline was looming, and everything seemed to be going wrong. That's exactly the kind of high-pressure situation I thrive in, and I've prepared examples to show you how I handle it.
examples.customer_facing: Have you ever felt completely overwhelmed by a confusing piece of technology? I remember when my own system crashed right before a big presentation, and I learned exactly how to turn chaos into calm for my customers.
examples.creator: What if I told you that the secret to viral content isn't luck, but a specific pattern of emotional vulnerability? I've analyzed thousands of successful videos, and I want to show you the formula I discovered.
examples.everyday: You know how sometimes you meet someone new and you just want to skip the small talk? Well, I actually have a story about a time I navigated a truly awkward social situation, and I think it relates to what we're discussing.

student.setup: You are presenting your research proposal for a final course project.
student.opening: Before you dive into the details, can you tell me what makes your approach to this topic stand out from everyone else's?

job_seeker.role: Hiring Manager for a tech firm
job_seeker.setup: You are in the final interview round for a challenging role.
job_seeker.opening: We've heard many strong resumes today; what unique perspective are you bringing to this role that sets you apart?

customer_facing.role: a frustrated customer on their third call
customer_facing.setup: A customer has already explained their problem to two people today. Now it's your turn.
customer_facing.opening: I've already explained this twice today. Before I go through it again, why should I believe you're the one who can fix it?

creator.role: Casting Director for a new series
creator.setup: You are pitching your unique concept for a new series to a director.
creator.opening: So many people are pitching ideas. What is the one surprising element in your concept that you think will grab the audience immediately?

everyday.setup: You are trying to start a meaningful conversation with someone you just met.
everyday.opening: Everyone here seems to know each other. What's one thing about yourself that you think would make people want to keep talking to you?

rubric.check: Their first sentence is a hook: a question, a short story, or a surprising fact (not 'Hi, my name is')
The hook connects to what they say next
Still makes clear who they are or what their idea is
